newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom may shed over 200 staff - NZPA.
newsitem.headline: Telecom may shed over 200 staff - NZPA.

text.p: More than 200 Telecom Corp of New Zealand workers will be made redundant throughout the country if staff cuts proposed by the company's management take effect on September 1, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Wednesday.

Telecom media communications manager Peter Brittenden told NZPA that 93 redundancies had been proposed for the South Island and 113 for the North Island. All workers affected would come from the design, build and maintenance (DBM) business unit.
He said Telecom had been signalling the cutbacks since late last year as part of a projected restructuring.
DBM management recognised the need to respond to a changing climate which included greater contestability and competition from private contractors for the work now carried out by the DBM unit.
The proposed staff cuts "were not set in concrete right now" and management were waiting for staff feedback.
"Who knows what staff members and groups of staff members will come back with?" Brittenden said.

Engineering, Printing and Manufacturing Union Wellington regional organiser Bruce Burnette said the Manawatu area, which includes Masterton, would lose 13 jobs, meaning staffing levels would drop to 85. Wanganui area would drop from 23 to 19.
Some workers intended to leave because they had "had a gutsful" of Telecom's constant restructuring, Burnette said.
He said the union would be ensuring that people got all their redundancy rights.
Deciding who will go has been left to local Telecom managers.
